root_cause.text: The stack-allocated `struct irdma_create_ah_resp` in `irdma_create_user_ah()` was not zero-initialized, so the reserved field `rsvd[4]` contained uninitialized kernel stack memory that was leaked to user space via `ib_respond_udata()`.
root_cause.evidence: The CVE description and commit message state: "rsvd[4]: 4 bytes of stack memory leaked unconditionally. Only ah_id is assigned before ib_respond_udata(). The reserved members of the structure were not zeroed." The patch fixes this by changing `struct irdma_create_ah_resp uresp;` to `struct irdma_create_ah_resp uresp = {};`.

intent_record.intent_summary: Zero-initialize the local response structure to avoid use of uninitialized stack memory.
intent_record.what: Changed declaration of `uresp` from uninitialized stack allocation to zero-initialization using `= {}`.
intent_record.how: This ensures all fields of the `struct irdma_create_ah_resp` are zeroed before any partial assignment or use, preventing potential undefined behavior from uninitialized data.

relevance_review.reason: The group directly addresses the vulnerability by zero-initializing the stack-allocated response structure, preventing uninitialized kernel stack memory from being leaked to user space.

candidates.rationale: This stack-allocated struct is not zero-initialized, so its reserved field 'rsvd[4]' contains uninitialized kernel stack memory, which is later copied to user space via ib_respond_udata(), causing an information leak.

bic_trace_step.reason: In the new function irdma_create_user_ah (lines 4271-4314), 'struct irdma_create_ah_resp uresp' is stack-allocated without zero-initialization. Only the 'ah_id' field is set before calling 'ib_copy_to_udata(udata, &uresp, min(sizeof(uresp), udata->outlen))'. The reserved fields (rsvd[4]) remain uninitialized, leaking kernel stack memory to userspace, which matches the root cause. No memset or zero-initializer is present, so the bug is introduced in this commit.
